paragraphs.text: This is [Dancong](dancong:name), the [oolong](oolong:definition) of [Phoenix Mountain](phoenix-mountain:where-it-is), a range in Fenghuang town in Chao'an, Chaozhou, in the east of Guangdong. Its name means single bush: the leaf of one bush picked and made on its own, from bushes chosen among the old Phoenix Shuixian plants of the mountain. Tea grows on these slopes from the low foothills up to roughly 1,100 metres. [Cloud and mist](phoenix-mountain:mist-and-climate) sit on the upper slopes for much of the year and the nights are cool, so the bushes grow slowly.

To make Dancong, the leaf is withered in the sun, shaken and rested in rounds, then [fixed fast at high heat, rolled into strips and roasted](dancong:making), traditionally over charcoal. A newly roasted Dancong is usually [rested for some months](dancong:ageing) before it is drunk. This leaf was made in 1950, so it has had seventy-six years.

brewing.text: Brew it gongfu style in a small gaiwan or clay pot, with about 3 to 8 grams for 100 to 120 ml and hot water, about 88 to 100°C; Chinese accounts mostly say 95 to 100°C. A quick rinse is common. Steeps start at a few seconds and grow a few seconds each round, and a good Dancong gives about eight to fifteen. Too long, too hot or too much leaf and it turns bitter and astringent.

notice.text: A smooth, mellow and sweet cup, often with dried fruit or plum and wood, sometimes something herbal, little astringency, and an amber to red-brown liquor.
